title: Regex Password Validator
description: Build a script that validates password strength using extended regular expressions.
problemStatement:
Write a script `pwcheck.sh` that reads a password from the user (silently) and checks the following criteria using regex and conditionals:

1. Must be at least 8 characters long.
2. Contains at least one uppercase letter.
3. Contains at least one lowercase letter.
4. Contains at least one digit.
5. Contains at least one special character from the set `@#$%^&+=`.

Use `[[ $pass =~ regex ]]` to test each requirement. Print each requirement as 'PASS' or 'FAIL' along with a reason. If all pass, print 'Strong password'. Otherwise, print 'Weak: fix the above'.

Ensure your regexes are correct: `[A-Z]`, `[a-z]`, `[0-9]`, `[@#$%^&+=]`. Use `read -sp` to hide input.

Bonus: add a loop that repeats until a strong password is entered.
hints: Use a variable `valid=true` and set to false if any check fails, or use individual flags.
expectedOutput:
Enter password: 
Length (8+): PASS
Uppercase letter: FAIL (missing)
Lowercase letter: PASS
Digit: PASS
Special char: FAIL (missing)
Weak: fix the above
solutionCode:
#!/bin/bash
# pwcheck.sh

valid=true
read -sp "Enter password: " pass
echo

# Length
if [ ${#pass} -lt 8 ]; then
  echo "Length (8+): FAIL (too short)"
  valid=false
else
  echo "Length (8+): PASS"
fi

# Uppercase
if [[ $pass =~ [A-Z] ]]; then
  echo "Uppercase letter: PASS"
else
  echo "Uppercase letter: FAIL (missing)"
  valid=false
fi

# Lowercase
if [[ $pass =~ [a-z] ]]; then
  echo "Lowercase letter: PASS"
else
  echo "Lowercase letter: FAIL (missing)"
  valid=false
fi

# Digit
if [[ $pass =~ [0-9] ]]; then
  echo "Digit: PASS"
else
  echo "Digit: FAIL (missing)"
  valid=false
fi

# Special
if [[ $pass =~ [@#\$%^&+=] ]]; then
  echo "Special char: PASS"
else
  echo "Special char: FAIL (missing)"
  valid=false
fi

if $valid; then
  echo "Strong password"
else
  echo "Weak: fix the above"
fi
